Simulate Bradley–Terry paired comparisons

Source: R/simulate_data.R
simulate_data.Rd

Generate synthetic paired comparisons from a standard Bradley–Terry model (model = "bt") or a model with shared block strengths (model = "bt-sbm"). Every unordered pair plays matches_per_pair matches. Given item strengths, pair counts are independent binomial draws, with probability lambda_i / (lambda_i + lambda_j) that item i wins.

Usage

simulate_data(
  model = c("bt", "bt-sbm"),
  latent_strength = NULL,
  n_blocks = NULL,
  players_per_block = 5L,
  matches_per_pair = 20L,
  item_labels = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  format = c("data", "edgelist", "matrix")
)

Arguments

model

Either "bt" (default) or "bt-sbm".

latent_strength

Positive generating strengths. Defaults to 20 distinct log-spaced item strengths from 12 to 1 for BT, or c(12, 6, 2, 1) for BT–SBM.

n_blocks

Number of generating blocks, for BT–SBM only. If NULL, inferred from the length of latent_strength.

players_per_block

Positive integer block sizes for BT–SBM: a scalar repeats one size, or a vector specifies each size separately.

matches_per_pair

Positive integer match count for every unordered pair.

item_labels

Optional unique item names. BT uses names on latent_strength when available, otherwise "Item 1", etc. BT–SBM retains the fictional tennis names used by tennis_tiered_toy().

seed

Integer random seed, or NULL to use the current random state.

format

Output representation: validated "data" (default), an aggregated "edgelist", or a win-count "matrix".

Value

Synthetic data in the requested representation. The "truth" attribute records generating item strengths, and block memberships for BT–SBM. Edge lists include both directions and zero counts.

Details

For BT, latent_strength supplies one fixed positive strength per item, aligned with item_labels before the output order is shuffled. For BT–SBM, it supplies one strength per generating block; memberships are randomly assigned to item names subject to the requested block sizes. These supplied strengths are not drawn from the Gamma prior used later for model fitting.

Examples

edges <- simulate_data("bt", latent_strength = c(A = 8, B = 3, C = 1),
                       matches_per_pair = 10, seed = 1, format = "edgelist")
as_bt_data(edges, format = "edgelist")
#> <btsbm_pairwise_data> 3 items and 30 wins
simulate_data("bt-sbm", latent_strength = c(8, 3, 1),
              players_per_block = c(2, 3, 4), seed = 1)
#> <btsbm_pairwise_data> 9 items and 720 wins
